agents.title: Build a geographic farm in any New Jersey town
agents.example: In Gloucester Township, start with a municipality-wide parcel set, then narrow by property class and layer assessment, sale and permit changes. A 56.95% 2026 Director's Ratio is context for assessment interpretation, not a lead score.
agents.limits: Public property records do not identify seller intent, financial distress, protected-class traits or whether an owner wants contact.

agents.title: Monitor the properties your past clients own
agents.query: real estate sphere of influence tracking
agents.example: An agent can attach known-client addresses from their CRM to Watchdog and monitor assessment, tax and permit changes while keeping identity and consent in the CRM.
agents.limits: Watchdog should not infer personal circumstances from property changes; the CRM remains the source of the relationship and consent.

agents.title: Work the circle around a recent New Jersey sale
agents.example: Use a verified recent sale as the center of a local research set, then compare surrounding assessments and recent verified-sale context before creating neighborhood-specific market content.
agents.limits: A nearby sale is market context, not proof that another property would sell for the same price.

agents.title: Research long-tenure properties in a farm area
agents.example: Where deed and sale-year history is supported, sort a farm by years since last recorded sale and then verify each record before outreach.
agents.limits: A long holding period does not imply age, equity, motivation, family status or likelihood to sell.

agents.title: Find properties affected by material tax change
agents.query: nj property tax increase by town
agents.example: Combine parcel tax history with municipal budget pressure so a tax increase can be explained in context instead of treated as a generic distress signal.
agents.limits: Budget pressure is a screening indicator, not a forecast of a specific future bill.

agents.title: Match a buyer need against New Jersey property records
agents.example: Build a property universe by geography, class, lot area or building attributes, then manually research likely fit before any lawful outreach through the agent's CRM.
agents.limits: Public property attributes do not establish willingness to sell or fair-housing-safe marketing eligibility.

agents.title: Build a small commercial property farm
agents.example: Track commercial-class parcels for assessment, sale and permit changes, then prioritize manual review when several independent property signals overlap.
agents.limits: Property records do not reveal business health, tenant circumstances or owner motivation.

agents.title: Stack independent Watchdog property signals
agents.example: A parcel with an assessment change, a recent permit and above-normal municipal tax pressure can be placed higher in a research queue because multiple property facts changed.
agents.limits: Signal stacking is prioritization for research, not a prediction about a person or transaction.

mortgage.title: Build a purchase-opportunity property territory
mortgage.example: Organize a territory around active agent relationships and monitor verified sale, assessment and property-record changes that create a reason for a property-side review.
mortgage.limits: Do not infer creditworthiness, income, eligibility or borrowing intent from property data.

mortgage.title: Review recent-purchase property cohorts
mortgage.query: recent home purchase follow up mortgage
mortgage.example: Track known clients or consented cohorts after purchase for material property-tax and assessment changes that may affect escrow conversations.
mortgage.limits: This is property servicing context, not a refinance solicitation trigger by itself.

mortgage.title: Translate assessment change into tax-payment context
mortgage.example: If a $300,000 assessment changes materially, compare the new assessment with the municipality's ratio and tax context before discussing possible escrow impact.
mortgage.limits: Only the tax authority and servicer determine the actual bill and escrow analysis.

mortgage.title: Monitor permitted improvement activity
mortgage.example: For an existing client relationship, a completed permit can trigger a property review to discuss updated value and financing needs without assuming the owner wants a loan.
mortgage.limits: A permit does not establish project cost, completion quality, borrowing intent or eligibility.

mortgage.title: Watch an investor property portfolio
mortgage.example: Group known investment properties by municipality and monitor tax, assessment, permit and sale-record changes in one property-side workspace.
mortgage.limits: Portfolio monitoring does not estimate borrower financial condition.

mortgage.title: Prepare a property-value refinance review
mortgage.example: Use verified sale ratios, assessment context and property attributes to identify records worth a manual value review, then use lender-approved valuation processes.
mortgage.limits: Watchdog is not an appraisal and does not determine loan eligibility.

mortgage.title: Share a property intelligence territory with an agent partner
mortgage.example: A lender and agent can work from the same geography and property changes while each keeps contact identity and consent in their own CRM.
mortgage.limits: The shared layer should contain property facts, not protected or inferred consumer traits.

mortgage.title: Monitor commercial property changes for lending research
mortgage.example: Monitor commercial parcels for transfers, improvements, assessment changes and environmental due-diligence flags before a relationship-based review.
mortgage.limits: Public property intelligence does not establish business creditworthiness or financing need.

mortgage.title: Build a client property-change desk
mortgage.example: Known-client properties can be watched for material assessment, permit and tax changes so a loan officer can provide timely service.
mortgage.limits: Alerts should be tied to an existing relationship or compliant outreach process.
